The bug is confirmed: `end = start + per_page - 1` makes the slice end exclusive-but-shifted-by-one, dropping the last item of each page. The fix is to make `end` the exclusive boundary: `start + per_page`.



Retrying (attempt 1/3, waiting 2s)...All tests pass. Quick edge-case sanity check, then done:

Retry finished, resuming.Done. Summary of the work:

**Bug:** In `toyapp/pagination.py`, the slice end index was `start + per_page - 1`. Since Python slice indices are exclusive on the right, this dropped the last item from every full page (page 1 of `["a","b","c","d"]` at per_page=2 returned only `["a"]`, not `["a","b"]`).

**Fix (1 line):** `end = start + per_page` — a single edit in `toyapp/pagination.py`. No clamping needed since Python slices handle out-of-range ends gracefully (partial last page, out-of-range pages, and empty input all behave correctly, verified).

**Checks run:**
- `pytest -q` via `/Users/instructor/Code/odsc-workshop/.workshop-venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` → **3 passed** (was 2 failed, 1 passed before the fix).
- Edge-case spot checks: partial last page (`['e']`), page beyond the end (`[]`), empty input (`[]`), and `page_numbers(5, 2)` → `[1, 2, 3]`.
- Final `git status` / `git diff` inspected (clean tree aside from the single intended modification).

**Files changed:** `toyapp/pagination.py` (1 line).

**Remaining uncertainty:** None. Tests were not modified; no dependencies installed; no commits made.
